title: lower_sound_full (lowering soundness WITH NOT, under Backend.Exact) is now machine-checked in core Lean; also lowerQ_sound_full with the tenant conjunct
summary: The r3 sorry is closed. Statement unchanged: ∀ B, B.Exact → ∀ r p b, sql3 B r (lower p) = some b → eval r p = b (pair invariant: a definite three-valued SQL answer equals the two-valued reference). Helper lemmas: anyEq_exact, beq_exact, brange_exact, bpfx_exact, k3and_some, k3or_some. Corollary lowerQ_sound_full: keeps B r (lowerQ tf t p) → refQ tf t r p for ALL p (no positivity side condition).
specifics: File /home/patrickd/aegis/research/state/raw/round-004/01-work/lean-golden/AegisIR/Lowering.lean (proof-only changes vs r3, semantics byte-identical). Added ~95 LOC of proof. Axioms of lower_sound_full / lowerQ_sound_full: {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}; k3and_some/k3or_some: {propext, Quot.sound}. Checked by Lean default kernel AND lake check --paranoid (leanchecker-paranoid, lean4lean, nanoda 0.4.19, con-leche, con-ron). Kleene lemmas proved by exhaustive `rcases a with _|⟨_|_⟩ <;> rcases c ... <;> cases b <;> simp_all` (27 cases).
overclaim_risk: Proves a MODEL of the lowering (mini SQL WHERE, single row, no joins/casts) — not the Rust renderer or the real engine; Exact is a hypothesis real engines violate (see r4e01.exact-vs-refines-not-witness).
underclaim_risk: The NOT fragment is fully discharged; the remaining risk is entirely in the adapter contract + rendering, which is where DRT must aim.
property: filter lowering soundness incl. NOT/NULL/empty IN
tcb: Lean kernel + 5 external checkers (any one correct)
llm_synthesizable: yes (written by an LLM agent in this run, 3 check iterations)

title: Machine-checked counterexample: Backend.Refines alone is INSUFFICIENT once NOT is in the IR; the R-DB-7 adapter contract must be two-sided (no leaks AND no misses) or NOT must be banned on that adapter
summary: Vacuity.refines_insufficient_for_not: a backend whose equality never matches (neverEq) satisfies Refines, yet lower (.not (.eq 1 (int 5))) keeps row1 while the policy eval is false. So completeness failures (backend says 'no' where reference says 'yes') become LEAKS under negation. Real instance of a completeness failure: PostgreSQL BUG #19645 (18.6, reported 2026-08-29): partition pruning on a text_pattern_ops key with a nondeterministic ICU collation drops matching rows (`WHERE c='b'` returns {2} not {1,2}; UPDATE/DELETE affect 1 row instead of 2).
specifics: Contract change for R-DB-7: (1) if the golden IR exposes Not (or any negative operator: ne, not-in, not-prefix), the adapter must ship Backend.Exact, i.e. the differential oracle reports leak_cases = 0 AND miss_cases = 0; (2) else the IR front end must statically reject Not for that adapter (lower_sound_pos covers the positive fragment under Refines only). Schema gate must also refuse partitioned tables whose partition-key opclass/collation differs from the column's (PG #19645/#19646 class).
overclaim_risk: neverEq is a toy; the PG bug is in pruning, not in the comparison operator, and needs an unusual schema.
underclaim_risk: Any optimizer-level wrong-result bug is an Exact violation; the PG bug list has a steady supply, so treating Refines as sufficient would silently admit NOT-based leaks.
property: necessity of two-sided atom contract under negation

title: Spec gap: the reference policy semantics is two-valued with absent⇒atom-false, so NOT over an absent/NULL field PERMITS; SQL hides it (UNKNOWN drops the row) but document stores implement it literally (MongoDB $ne matches documents lacking the field)
summary: Lowering.not_absent_permits: r f = none → eval r (.not (.eq f v)) = true. The SQL lowering stays sound (stricter), but the REFERENCE grants rows a policy author would read as 'owner ≠ alice' = only rows with a different owner. MongoDB docs: $ne 'selects documents where the value of the field is not equal to the specified value. This includes documents that do not contain the field.' A Mongo adapter that is Exact w.r.t. this reference is therefore exactly as permissive as the reference.
specifics: Decision needed (flagged, NOT applied — would be a spec change): either (a) make the reference three-valued (eval : Row → Pred → Option Bool, permit iff some true, matching SQL and Cedar's error⇒deny), re-proving lower_sound_full as equality of Option Bool; or (b) forbid Not over nullable/optional fields at IR type-check time; for Mongo additionally require {$exists:true} guards on every negated field. Recommendation: (a) — it aligns all adapters with SQL and Cedar semantics and removes the asymmetry.
overclaim_risk: Whether it is a bug depends on intended policy semantics; some authors want 'not owned by alice' to include unowned rows.
underclaim_risk: Silent widening on optional attributes is the classic authz bug class (Cedar made missing-attribute an error for this reason).

title: Token T1-T6 transcribed into core Lean and CHECKED: 16 theorems (attenuation monotonicity, audience binding, expiry incl. effective-min, depth non-increase + verify-time bound, verify_iff, holder attenuation MAC correctness, enc injectivity from canonical codec)
summary: AegisIR/Token.lean. T1 attenuation_mono / attenuation_mono_append; T2 aud_bound; T3 expiry_minted, effExp_append, effExp_append_exp, expiry_effective; T4 effDepth_append, effDepth_append_le, depthOk_bound; T5 verify_iff, attenuate_mac, attenuate_narrows; T6 Codec structure + enc_injective, parse_canonical. HMAC is a universally-quantified parameter H (not an axiom/opaque), so nothing enters the TCB; EUF-CMA is an explicit external assumption.
specifics: Axioms: T1/T4/T5 propext only; T2/T3/attenuate_mac {propext, Quot.sound}; enc_injective, parse_canonical: none. Build 1.25 s / 498 MB (single file). SKEPTIC NOTES: verify_iff is definitional (unfold+simp) — security content is zero without EUF-CMA; T6 proves only 'roundtrip ⇒ injective', the roundtrip itself is cborrs/EverParse's (cited, not re-proven, not linked to Lean); `verify` does NOT check WellMinted, so T2/T3 apply only if the issuer is the sole origin of chain heads (true under EUF-CMA) — defense-in-depth fix: add a mint-shape check to verify and prove `verify → r.aud = a ∧ r.now < e` directly (next obligation, ~20 LOC).
overclaim_risk: Checks a model of the token; the Rust verifier, CBOR codec, constant-time compare and HMAC are outside the proof.
underclaim_risk: T1/T5' (attenuation never widens even with adversarial appends) is the core macaroon property and is now kernel-checked with zero custom axioms.
tcb: Lean kernel; EUF-CMA(HMAC-SHA256) assumed; cborrs codec (EverParse) cited

title: Transcription forced 4 token spec decisions the r3 prose left ambiguous: segment-prefix resources (D1), op bitmask subset (D2), depth enforced at VERIFY time not append time (D3), absent tool argument denies (D4)
summary: D1: res_prefix must be a path-SEGMENT prefix (List String), checked witness segment_prefix_blocks_t10 (['t1'] does not admit ['t10','doc']); a string prefix would admit /t1 → /t10. D3: r3 said 'appending is allowed only if depth_left > 0' — unenforceable in an HMAC chain because holders append offline; the verifier enforces caveats_after_mint ≤ minted depth (depthOk: length ≤ 3 + effDepth, min over appended depth caveats); witness depth_enforced. D4 fail-closed on missing argument keys. D2 r.ops &&& mask = r.ops.
specifics: Rust obligations derived: verifier splits canonical path into segments exactly like the model (no trailing-slash/empty-segment ambiguity: canonicaliser rejects '//' and trailing '/'); kid fixed 8 B and nonce fixed 16 B so kid||nonce concatenation is unambiguous; F6 depth_matrix fuzz target must include 'append beyond depth' (expect reject).
overclaim_risk: D1-D4 are choices; ratification belongs to the spec freeze.
underclaim_risk: D1 is a real cross-tenant bug class if left as string prefix.

title: Since Lean 4.29 native_decide asserts a per-theorem axiom named `<thm>._native.native_decide.ax_N_M`; 4.35.0 removed Lean.ofReduceBool/trustCompiler entirely — so axiom gates that DENYLIST ofReduceBool silently pass native_decide; only an ALLOWLIST is correct
summary: Observed in the negative control: `#print axioms AegisIR.Bad.uses_native` → 'AegisIR.Bad.uses_native._native.native_decide.ax_1_1' (no ofReduceBool). PR #14953 (merged 2026-08-28) 'removes Lean.reduceBool, Lean.reduceNat, Lean.ofReduceBool, Lean.ofReduceNat and Lean.trustCompiler'; Lean reference ValidatingProofs: 'Since Lean 4.29.0, each native computation gets its own axiom'. Prior gate specs in this map (vfg-proof-ci-gate-spec grep list) and external project policies (CompPoly AGENTS.md: 'must not depend on Lean.ofReduceBool') are stale for ≥4.29.
specifics: Gate rule: allowlist {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}; fail on anything else, including any name containing '_native'. Note Classical.choice cannot be dropped: even `rfl` theorems over our definitions (orN_nil) report Classical.choice via Init definitions (String/List decidability).
overclaim_risk: Source-level grep for native_decide still catches direct uses; the hole is for gates relying on axiom names alone.
underclaim_risk: A silent false-PASS in the proof gate is the worst failure mode named in R-FORMAL-3.

title: lake check's bwrap sandbox fails out of the box on Ubuntu 24.04 (AppArmor restricts unprivileged user namespaces): 'bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied'
summary: Observed on this laptop: Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1, no bwrap profile in /etc/apparmor.d → lake check exits before building. Workarounds: an AppArmor profile granting `userns` to /usr/bin/bwrap (needs root, forbidden here), the sysctl (weakens host), or --inadvisably-no-sandbox (PR #15156, 2026-09-14), which is acceptable ONLY for first-party sources we wrote. lake check exit code 2 is 'could not start'; here bwrap's failure surfaced as 'error: Child exited with 1' (exit 1) — a CI wrapper must not conflate it with a proof rejection.
specifics: Golden CI: run the paranoid gate on a runner where bwrap works (GitHub-hosted runner status for ubuntu-24.04 not verified — spike), or in a VM and use `lake check --from-export` ONLY on exports we generated. For third-party contributions: sandbox mandatory, never --inadvisably-no-sandbox.
overclaim_risk: Host-specific; other distros/runners may allow userns.
underclaim_risk: The most common developer distro breaks the 'gold-standard' check by default; teams will reach for the no-sandbox flag.

title: Kernel trusts built-in prelude declarations by NAME (Nat.add etc.): an export that redefines them proves False axiom-free and passes both Lean kernels — Lean FRO classifies it as adversarial input, not a bug; only comparator-style prelude comparison catches it
summary: lean4 issue #15908 (2026-10-24, closed same day): export with a non-canonical Nat.add yields axiom-free `contra : False`; 'both Lean default and Lean paranoid accept'. Maintainer: 'not a kernel soundness bug... Your export replaces the official prelude's Nat.add'; comparator rejects ('Const does not match between challenge and target Nat.add'). Soundness-report guide (hackmd, targets v4.35.0): 'We treat an alternative prelude as an adversarial input'.
specifics: Gate policy: `lake check --from-export` is allowed only on exports built by our own pinned toolchain from our sources; any externally produced proof/export (agent marketplace, contractor, cloud prover) goes through `lake comparator` with our challenge file (statement + prelude matching) and the sandbox. Note this hole is in the export trust model, not in lake build of source.
overclaim_risk: Requires an attacker who controls the export file; irrelevant for first-party builds.
underclaim_risk: Exactly the setting of cloud-agent-written proofs accepted as artifacts (§0c) if artifacts rather than sources are accepted.

title: Lean kernel/checker soundness record 2026: two axiom-free proofs of False fixed in July (4.32.1, 4.32.2), two kernel use-after-free fixes in 4.35.0, two leanchecker acceptance bugs (Sep) — pin ≥4.35.0 and keep multi-kernel checking

New compiler miscompilation #10925 (2025-10) is the native_decide risk class. Labels 'soundness' and 'runtime-soundness' exist on lean4.

Implication: golden pins toolchain ≥4.35.0, subscribes to security@lean-fro.org advisories, and requires all six checkers (independent implementations: C++, Lean, Rust nanoda, con-leche, con-ron) to accept.

title: Spec-fidelity audit: every hypothesis of every theorem, whether the Rust implementation could violate it, and the vacuity check (concrete models satisfy all hypotheses, so False is not derivable from them)
summary: VACUITY: Vacuity.lean exhibits models: refBackend satisfies Exact (hence Refines); keeps_nonvacuous (lowerQ keeps a real row with a NOT filter); token_nonvacuous (WellMinted ∧ denote ∧ depthOk all true); combine_nonvacuous. A satisfying model is a semantic consistency proof of the hypothesis set — no theorem is vacuously true. LOWERING hypotheses: (h : B.Refines/Exact) — VIOLABLE by every real engine config (collation, affinity, PAD SPACE, LIKE wildcards, optimizer wrong-results like PG #19645) → per-adapter DRT two-sided + schema gate; (p.positive) — violable if the IR front end lets Not through on a Refines-only adapter → make it a type-level restriction; MODEL ASSUMPTIONS not stated as hypotheses but equally load-bearing: Rust `lower` = Lean `lower` (renderer could mis-parenthesise, render IN [] as invalid SQL, or bind NULL) → DRT Lean-compiled lower vs Rust AST (structural, not strings); Value has no NULL literal → Rust IR must not admit NULL literals; single-row WHERE only (no joins/subqueries/casts/aggregates) → IR must not express them on this path; tenant value t is 'host-minted' — the theorem holds for ANY t, binding t to the authenticated principal is a separate capability obligation. TOKEN hypotheses: WellMinted — issuer obligation; Lean `verify` does not check it, so a mis-minting issuer voids T2/T3 → add mint-shape check to Rust verify and to the Lean verify; H parameter — EUF-CMA assumed; Codec roundtrip — cborrs; kid/nonce fixed lengths — Rust must enforce or kid||nonce is ambiguous. COMBINE: host maps crash/timeout to error before combine — DST obligation.
